What a Price Target Really Means

A price target is an analyst's estimate of where a stock should trade in about 12 months, built from forecasts for earnings, growth and a reasonable valuation multiple. Upside is simply the gap between today's share price and the average of those targets, expressed as a percentage. Because targets are opinions rather than guarantees, they can move quickly after a company reports, and a cut does not always mean the analyst has turned negative. Sometimes a firm trims its target to reflect a stock that has already risen, or an expectations bar that was set too high, while keeping a positive rating.

That is why the rating and the target are best read together. An upgrade with a lower target tells a different story from a reiterated rating with a higher one. The reasons behind a change, such as delayed contracts, better cost control or a pricing shift, usually say more than the number does. Ranking by average upside adds a second layer. A large gap to the average target can point to a stock that has fallen out of favor as easily as to one analysts expect to take off. Our list of NYSE-listed stocks with large analyst-estimated upside shows how wide that spread can get on a single exchange. Following the reasons as well as the numbers keeps that distinction clear.

detail:
Stock Market Today, Nov. 19: Dow Plunges 1,100 Points as the S&P 500 Suffers Its 6th Straight Day of Losses
RJ Fulton, The Motley Fool
Thu, November 19, 2026 at 2:10 PM PST 3 min read
^GSPC
INSM
SNY
^DJI
GC=F
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Wall Street's sell-off intensified on Thursday, November 19, as selling pressure spread across nearly every sector of the market. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJINDICES:^DJI) plunged more than 1,100 points, falling 2.19% to 49,097 and moving closer to correction territory. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 2.00% to 7,177, marking its sixth consecutive session of losses, while the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) dropped 2.23% to 23,886 as investors continued to retreat from growth stocks.

Selling pressure extended beyond equities, with gold falling 2.10% to $3,663.50. The 10-year Treasury yield eased three basis points to 5.07%, offering little relief to equity markets. Energy and consumer staples were among the few sectors to finish in positive territory, gaining 0.14% and 0.04%, respectively, while industrials plunged 2.61%.

Today's biggest moves

Despite the broader market sell-off, Insmed (NASDAQ:INSM) surged 20.58% following reports that French pharmaceutical giant Sanofi (NASDAQ:SNY) is considering an acquisition of the biotechnology company. Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW) also bucked the broader trend, gaining 6.42% after reporting stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings and announcing a $4.5 billion acquisition.

Conversely, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) plunged 7.72% following a media report alleging ties to a blacklisted Chinese server manufacturer. The report adds another layer of regulatory uncertainty to a semiconductor industry already grappling with tightening U.S. export restrictions and deteriorating investor sentiment.

What this means for investors

Perhaps the most concerning development on Wall Street is how broadly selling pressure has spread. What initially appeared to be a pullback driven by elevated technology valuations is increasingly developing into a broader market downturn. Even Nvidia's (NASDAQ:NVDA) exceptional quarterly earnings have failed to reverse sentiment, suggesting that concerns surrounding inflation, interest rates, and stock valuations are taking precedence over strong corporate results.

Looking ahead, investors should pay particularly close attention to Treasury yields and the U.S. dollar. With the Federal Reserve signaling that further interest rate hikes may be necessary, persistently restrictive financial conditions could put additional pressure on corporate earnings and stock valuations heading into 2027.

Walmart's (NASDAQ:WMT) upcoming quarterly earnings report will also provide an important assessment of consumer spending heading into the holiday shopping season. While recent results from Target (NYSE:TGT) and TJX Companies, Inc. (NYSE:TJX) have been encouraging, any signs of weakening consumer demand could introduce another headwind for equities.

All 20 tech stocks on a list from financial newsletter The Kobeissi Letter trade at least 25% below record highs. CoreWeave (CRWV) leads the slide at 76%.

Additionally, the S&P 500 has lost over $6 trillion in six weeks adding pressure to the markets in general. The Nasdaq Composite, however, sits in correction territory, a 10% decline, not the 20% that defines a bear market.

Why Are Cloud and Chip Names Falling Hardest?

The deepest drops cluster in cloud computing, chips, and data storage. Oracle (ORCL) and SanDisk (SNDK), a flash memory maker, each trail their highs by 68%. Nebius (NBIS), an artificial intelligence (AI) cloud provider, is down 66%.

Intel (INTC) is down 61%. Western Digital (WDC), a data storage maker, and Arm (ARM), a chip designer, each trail by 60%. Tesla (TSLA) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) show the mildest declines at 25%, still beyond the 20% bear market line.

CoreWeave, which rents computing capacity to AI developers, grew third-quarter revenue 168% to $3.66 billion. Its net loss still reached $709 million, with net interest expense at $846 million, according to its results.

A correction means a 10% decline from a record, while a bear market requires 20%. The Nasdaq Composite closed at 23,879.20 on Nov. 19. That sits below the 24,315.00 close that confirmed its correction on Nov. 5, CNBC reported.

Meanwhile, the S&P 500 fell 2.02% on Nov. 19 to 7,175.83. AMD fell further after short seller Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a bet against the chipmaker.

Will the Indexes Follow These Tech Stocks Lower?

The Kobeissi Letter, meanwhile, has described the selloff as a historic opportunity. In both earlier 2026 episodes, in March and July, the Composite later set new records, a Motley Fool analysis shows.

If that pattern holds, indexes could recover while these 20 stocks lag. A close 20% below the Oct. 6 record, however, would most likely break it.

title: Is Indonesia Holding Back Freeport-McMoRan Stock?
detail:
Is Indonesia Holding Back Freeport-McMoRan Stock?
Trefis Team
Thu, November 19, 2026 at 2:01 PM PST 4 min read
FCX
^GSPC
HG=F
Trade FCX on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: Could Anthropic Stock Fall 25%?

For Freeport-McMoRan (FCX), the answer depends on how fast its Grasberg mine in Indonesia gets back to full speed. In 2025, the Indonesia segment was the one large part of the company where sales shrank, falling by 16.4%. Shareholders have had a rough month as well. The stock lost 25.3% in the month to November 18, 2026, against a 5.0% fall for the S&P 500.

If one of those shareholders sent the Indonesia team a note this week, it would be short. What would it say?

Freeport-McMoRan shares lost 25.3% in a single month. If this copper miner is a big part of your savings, a drop like that is hard to sleep through. The Trefis Income Solution fell less than the S&P 500 in each of the 9 big sell-offs since 2018, and it pays a dividend yield about 3 times the S&P 500's. See how it held up.

A Note From Freeport's Owners To The Indonesia Team

Your business made up a third of Freeport-McMoRan's sales in 2025. The segment brought in $8.62 billion that year, 33.3% of company revenue. All the other segments together grew about 14% that year, to $17.3 billion. So in 2025 the rest of Freeport carried you, a year after your own sales rose 22.3%.

We ask only that you deliver the plan you already set. The Grasberg Block Cave ran at 67% of mine capacity in the third quarter of 2026. Management targets 80% by mid-2027 and close to full capacity by the end of 2027. Those dates are the promise your owners will hold you to.

Freeport's Indonesia Business Faces Water And Delays

Water is one challenge right now. Indonesia has had abnormally dry weather, management said on the October 27, 2026 call. Dry ground is generally good for mining. But low water makes it hard to raise mill rates, the speed at which the mills process ore. Management expects more normal conditions as 2027 begins, based on weather forecasts.

The next mine is also running late. Freeport is somewhat behind on development at Kucing Liar, which is expected to start ramping up in the 2029 to 2030 timeframe. Freeport expects to spend about $1.6 billion on discretionary projects in 2026 and $2 billion in 2027. Roughly half of this spending goes to Kucing Liar and the liquefied natural gas (LNG) project at Grasberg.

What Is Going Right At Freeport-McMoRan?

Plenty is going right, starting in the U.S. Operating income at Freeport's U.S. mining operations more than doubled in the third quarter of 2026 from a year earlier. For the whole company, the operating margin rose to 31.2% that quarter from 28.1% a year before, and net income reached $1.17 billion, up from $0.674 billion.
